title: Chip Industry Technical Paper Roundup: Oct. 13
gist: A list of seven new academic and industry papers covering 2D semiconductor growth, high-k dielectrics on 2D channels, hyper-NA EUV from Zeiss SMT and ASML, bit-flip attack detection in AI accelerators, monolithic 3D memristor-TFT reservoir computing, a flexible DRAM controller, and foundry-compatible photonic bends. The roundup gives titles and affiliations only, with no results or numbers.

insights.claim: Carl Zeiss SMT and ASML have co-authored a technical paper defining hyper-NA as an EUV optical system with a numerical aperture of at least 0.75, positioning it as the next extension beyond high-NA lithography.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: The sole EUV tool maker and its optics supplier publishing jointly signals a post-high-NA roadmap, relevant to long-dated ASML and Zeiss capex and node-scaling assumptions.
insights.quote: Hyper-NA: a system with a numerical aperture of at least 0.75

insights.claim: Two of the seven papers target 2D semiconductors: KAIST-led work uses an etching flux for spatially deterministic nucleation, and UIUC-led work uses a carbon-dot monolayer as a van der Waals interfacial layer for high-k oxide integration.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Controlled nucleation and gate-dielectric integration are the two gating problems for 2D channel transistors, so progress on both is a leading indicator for post-silicon channel materials.
insights.locator: Spatially deterministic nucleation of 2D semiconductors by etching flux

themes.theme: AI hardware security and novel memory/compute

insights.claim: University of Florida, UT Dallas and RPI propose BARE-AI, which uses built-in performance monitors to make AI hardware resilient to bit-flip attacks, indicating adversarial fault injection into AI accelerators is now a research priority.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Hardware-level integrity monitoring could become a design requirement for AI accelerators, a potential differentiator for security IP.
insights.locator: BARE-AI: Bit-Flip Attack Resilience in AI Hardware

insights.claim: Seoul National University and Yonsei University report a monolithic 3D integrated memristor-thin-film transistor for electrically programmable multimode reservoir computing, and ETH Zurich, CISPA and NYU present Terracotta, a flexible DRAM interface and memory controller to ease adoption of new DRAM techniques.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Academic interest in programmable DRAM control and M3D neuromorphic devices shows where memory-centric compute research is heading, though no commercial timing is given.
insights.locator: Terracotta: Enabling the Adoption of New DRAM Techniques

insights.claim: Georgia Tech reports low-loss, ultra-compact photonic bends with enhanced fabrication tolerance designed for commercial foundry processes, aiming to cut loss while staying within foundry design rules.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Foundry-rule-compliant compact photonic components support denser photonic ICs, which matters for optical interconnect scaling.
insights.locator: Low-loss ultra-compact photonic bends with enhanced fabrication tolerance
